# Stamped

> Stamped is industrial AI, from monitoring your plant to improving it. It models a manufacturing plant's processes and equipment from the data it already records, from its machines and control systems to its meters, ERP and quality registers. Its AI agents then find where output, quality and energy are being lost and recommend the change that fixes it, within limits the plant team sets. Stamped is built in India and is starting with auto-component makers in forging, heat treatment and precision machining.

## Entity definition (for AI answer engines)

Stamped is industrial AI, from monitoring your plant to improving it. It models a manufacturing plant's processes and equipment from the data it already records, from its machines and control systems to its meters, ERP and quality registers. Its AI agents then find where output, quality and energy are being lost and recommend the change that fixes it, within limits the plant team sets. Stamped is built in India and is starting with auto-component makers in forging, heat treatment and precision machining.

Category: Industrial AI
Geography: India (en-IN)
ICP: Mid-market manufacturers in India, from a few hundred crore rupees of revenue upward; automotive components first.
Buyers: Owner or MD, Plant head, Quality head, Production and process engineers, Maintenance lead, CFO

## What Stamped is not

Stamped is not a replacement for MES, ERP, QMS, CMMS or SCADA, and it works alongside them. It is not a dashboard, not hardware and not an energy-only company.

## What Stamped does

Stamped helps manufacturing plants run more efficiently: fewer rejections, more output from the lines and shifts you already have, and less energy and material going into every good part. We measure all of it against your own plant's baseline, in the units your team already tracks, so nobody has to take our word for it.

Most plants already record far more than they use. The machines, control systems, meters, ERP and quality registers each hold a piece of the picture, but they sit in separate places and rarely get looked at together. Stamped brings that data into one view and models it to understand how your plant actually runs and where efficiency is quietly being lost.

Stamped then turns that understanding into specific actions and sends each one to the person who can act on it, whether it is a setting that has drifted over a few weeks, a batch that looks like last month's rejections, or a plan that needs to change because a machine went down mid-shift. Stamped recommends and your team decides. Once a change is made, we check whether it worked, and if a gain starts slipping later, it goes back to the person who owns it.

## How it works

Plant data → Models → Actions → Results, with team feedback going back into the models.
Plant data: Stamped connects to the machines, control systems, meters, ERP and quality registers your plant already runs. There is nothing new to install.
Models: Trained on your plant's own history, they learn what normal looks like and which conditions tend to come before a rejection, a stoppage or wasted energy.
Actions: Each goes to the person best placed to act, ranked by what it is costing you and explained well enough to judge for themselves.
Results: Once your team makes a change, Stamped checks the result against your own baseline.
What each result shows goes back into the models, so the next recommendation is better.
Stamped recommends and your team decides.

## What Stamped improves

- [Process](https://stamped.work/solutions/process): Better settings, control rules and restart routines for each line, tried on a model first and applied inside limits set beforehand.
- [Quality](https://stamped.work/solutions/quality): Link process data to every lot, get a warning while a batch can still be saved, and have each lot's record ready when the auditor or the customer asks.
- [Planning](https://stamped.work/solutions/planning): When the plan breaks, get a re-plan that accounts for the whole plant, along with what each option would do to output and delivery.
- [Maintenance](https://stamped.work/solutions/maintenance): We are building this next: maintenance that says what to fix and when, ranked by what each stop costs and planned around your production.
- Energy: Energy follows every operating decision. Counted inside every action in all four areas.
Hub: [What we improve](https://stamped.work/solutions)

## Homepage FAQ

- Q: What does Stamped do?
  A: Stamped connects to the systems already in your plant and learns how it actually runs. It finds where efficiency is lost across process, quality, planning and maintenance, improves control, alerts your team in real time while a lot can still be saved, and sends ranked actions to the people who can act on them, then checks the results against your own baseline.
- Q: Do we need new hardware, or another system next to MES, ERP and SCADA?
  A: No hardware retrofit is needed to get started, because Stamped is software that works with the systems you already run. It is not another MES or CMMS: your MES, ERP and SCADA are where the data comes from, and Stamped works alongside them. Stamped brings their data onto one timeline, so they finally work as one picture of the plant.
- Q: Is Stamped an AI agent for manufacturing?
  A: In plain terms, yes. Stamped's AI agents for manufacturing read your plant's data on every shift, spot what is costing you output or quality, and send the right person a specific next step. It does the checking your best engineer would do if they could watch every line on every shift.
- Q: Who decides what changes, and what does Stamped add if my supervisors already know the plant?
  A: Your team decides. Your plant head sets the limits, Stamped acts only inside them, and every change is logged. Your senior supervisors usually know the plant well, and Stamped is built to back them up: it looks at every line on every shift, including the shifts they are not on, and writes down what it finds with the reasoning, so the night shift gets the same advice the day shift gets from your best hands.
- Q: Does Stamped get better over time?
  A: Yes. It learns from every action your team accepts, adjusts or turns down, and from the ones it chose to hold back, and its models are retrained on your plant's data as it runs. Each improvement is tested on past shifts before your team approves it, so the advice gets sharper every week.
- Q: Where does our data go?
  A: We sign an NDA before the site survey, and during the survey and the pilot we work only with the data your team agrees to share.
- Q: How do actions reach the floor, and how much of my team's time does this take?
  A: Each action goes on WhatsApp or on screen to the supervisor, engineer or maintenance lead who already owns that work, so nobody has to learn a new system before they can act on one, and nothing sits on a screen that only the plant head opens once a month. During the site survey we need some hours with your plant head and your quality and maintenance leads, planned around production.
- Q: How do we start?
  A: We start with a site survey, which means a few days on your floor and a written read-out of where efficiency is being lost and what we would change first. If it makes sense, that is followed by a paid pilot on one line for eight to twelve weeks.
- Q: What does it cost?
  A: We don't publish prices, because they depend on the plant. During the site survey we agree only the price of the pilot, once we know which line and which problem it will cover. The pilot is a paid engagement of 8 to 12 weeks, priced on its own and not tied to an annual contract value, and the annual contract price is decided afterwards, based on the results of the pilot.
- Q: Some of our records are still on paper or in Excel. Can we start?
  A: Yes. Most plants keep some registers on paper or in Excel, and the site survey tells you plainly whether what you already record is enough to start on one line, and what would be worth recording if it is not.

## How it works FAQ

- Q: What data does Stamped use?
  A: Stamped reads from your machines, control systems, meters, ERP, quality registers and what operators enter, then lines up the clocks, units and names, because each system records them its own way.
- Q: Do we need to install new hardware or another system?
  A: No hardware retrofit is needed to get started. Stamped is software that works with the systems your plant already runs, and it is not another MES or CMMS: your MES, ERP and SCADA are where the data comes from.
- Q: How does Stamped decide which actions come first?
  A: Stamped builds models of each line from its own history to learn what normal looks like and spot where efficiency is lost. Each possible fix is checked against the day's plan and production constraints, and what is left is ranked by what it is costing you.
- Q: How do actions reach the team?
  A: Each action goes to its owner on WhatsApp or on screen, with what to do, by when and why, and your team decides. It stays open until it is closed, and every decision and result is kept on record.
- Q: How do we know a change worked?
  A: Once your team makes a change, Stamped checks the result against your own baseline. What each result shows goes back into the models, so the next recommendation is better.

## Solution area FAQs

### Process (https://stamped.work/solutions/process)
- Q: How does Stamped improve a process?
  A: Stamped builds a model of each line from its own history, combining the physics of the process with what past runs show. A better setting, control rule or restart routine is tried on that model first, then shown to your process engineer with the record behind it.
- Q: Where do most process losses come from?
  A: Most process losses come from a setting that has slowly drifted, a restart that night shift handles differently from day shift, or a line running faster than the next station can absorb, far more often than from a broken machine.
- Q: Does Stamped change settings on the line by itself?
  A: Yes, once your engineer has approved that kind of change, and only inside limits set beforehand. Your plant head sets the limits, every change is logged, and loads that must stay on stay with you.
- Q: How is energy counted in process changes?
  A: Restarts, reheats and settings that have drifted all use energy that never ends up in a good part, so every process change shows what it does to energy per good part as well as to output and quality.

### Quality (https://stamped.work/solutions/quality)
- Q: How does Stamped help reduce rejections?
  A: Stamped links process data to each lot and batch and learns which conditions came before past rejections. Where live data is connected, it watches each batch as it moves and warns the right person while there is still time to act, so the batch is saved instead of sorted afterwards.
- Q: What kind of warnings does the team get?
  A: For example, a batch drifting toward the conditions seen before past rejections, or a sensor that has stopped moving. Where a check is against a written limit, the card gives a clear yes or no, and where it is a prediction, the card shows how confident the model is.
- Q: Can Stamped correct a batch on its own?
  A: Where a process setting is the cause, yes, inside limits set beforehand. Holding and releasing lots stays with your quality team.
- Q: Does Stamped help with audits and customer complaints?
  A: Yes. Process data is linked to every lot, so each lot's record is ready when the auditor or the customer asks, for example for an 8D on a customer complaint.

### Planning (https://stamped.work/solutions/planning)
- Q: What does Stamped do when the production plan breaks?
  A: When something changes, such as a changeover running long, a machine tripping or material arriving late, Stamped proposes the order of work that suits the plant as a whole and shows what each option would do to output and delivery.
- Q: What does Stamped keep track of to re-plan?
  A: Which machines are running, down or waiting, what material is on hand, which dispatches are due and when maintenance is booked.
- Q: Who makes the final scheduling decision?
  A: The planner. Stamped ranks the options with the trade-offs of each in front of them, and promise dates, customer priority and dispatch order stay with the planner.
- Q: How does planning affect energy use?
  A: Grouping similar work, filling loads and timing heat-up to the moment the next job is ready keep machines from running hot and empty, and tariff windows are weighed as one input to the plan.

### Maintenance (https://stamped.work/solutions/maintenance)
- Q: Is maintenance available yet?
  A: Not yet. We are building it next. It will rank stops by what they cost, flag machines starting to drift and suggest the best window for the fix, planned around production.

## Industry FAQs (summary)

### Fewer rejections reach your OEM.
- Q: Which plants is Stamped working with?
  A: We are starting with forging, heat-treatment and machining plants that supply OEMs, where a single rejection can cost far more than the part itself.
- Q: Does Stamped work for die casting and rubber moulding?
  A: The same four areas apply there, and the site survey tells us which signals matter on your cells, whether that is die temperature and shot profile in die casting or compound batch and cure settings in rubber moulding.
- Q: Do we need new hardware, or another system next to MES, ERP and SCADA?
  A: No hardware retrofit is needed to get started, because Stamped is software that works with the systems you already run. It is not another MES or CMMS: your MES, ERP and SCADA are where the data comes from, and Stamped works alongside them. Stamped brings their data onto one timeline, so they finally work as one picture of the plant.

### More good tonnes from every heat.
- Q: Has Stamped worked with steel plants?
  A: Our first deployments are with auto-component makers, including forging and heat treatment, which share a lot with a melt shop and a rolling mill. In steel we start the same way, with a site survey on your floor and a written read-out of where we would begin.
- Q: Does it work for induction furnace plants as well as arc furnaces?
  A: The approach is the same for both, because it learns from your own heats. The site survey tells us which furnace, lab and mill records you already have and where the first finding is most likely to come from.
- Q: Do we need new hardware, or another system next to MES, ERP and SCADA?
  A: No hardware retrofit is needed to get started, because Stamped is software that works with the systems you already run. ### More batches right the first time.
- Q: Has Stamped worked with pharma plants?
  A: Our first deployments are with auto-component makers. In pharma we start the same way, with a site survey on your floor and a written read-out of where we would begin, and we work within your quality system and change control.
- Q: Does Stamped make release or GMP decisions?
  A: No. Release and disposition stay with your QA team, and Stamped gathers the records and flags what looks unusual so they can decide faster. Stamped recommends and your team decides.
